items.title: Establish the migration contract and what stays frozen
items.context: Before touching anything, write the decision doc that answers: which identities move, which stay frozen and why, and how each moved identity handles pre-existing on-disk state. Must explicitly confirm and cite that lattice-*-integrity-v1 salts, and the 13 lattice-* agent role IDs, are NOT in scope. Must decide the read-both policy per item: a resolver that accepts the old path/name for reading while writing only the new one, versus a hard cutover with a one-time migration. Establishes the acceptance criterion that 326 story archives under .lattice/story/actives remain readable and their signatures still verify after migration.
items.userSees: docs/requirements/decisions/proof-or-stop-identity-migration.md exists and `grep -c "storyFilesHash"` prints a count >= 1, with a line reading "PATHS ARE HASHED" citing story-files-hash-material-drift.md:30-31

happy.desc: grep -c storyFilesHash on the new decision doc prints "1" or higher

edge.desc: The doc names an identity with NO verdict recorded and the CHK-001 self-check catches it before DEV proceeds

adversarial.desc: A reader cannot conclude a FROZEN row was silently ignored: both supersessions (@lattice/core, bin aliases) appear with citations

items.title: Add a read-both path resolver for the state directory before moving any file
items.context: 193+ code sites reference the literal '.lattice'. Introduce a single resolver (extending the core/brand-env.ts additive pattern from B-cdf6) that resolves the state dir, adapter dir, and config filenames, accepting the deprecated name for READS and writing only the canonical name. Land this FIRST so the codebase can operate on either layout; that makes the actual move reversible instead of a flag day. Route every literal through the resolver.
items.userSees: `node bin/proof-or-stop.js session_brief` prints "Checklist-derived ledger" with .lattice still on disk, and `grep -rn "'.lattice'" packages/*/src` returns only the resolver file

happy.desc: node bin/proof-or-stop.js session_brief prints the story ledger while .lattice is still the on-disk name

edge.desc: A project with NEITHER state dir present fails with a clear message naming the canonical path, not a stack trace

adversarial.desc: grep -rn "'\.lattice'" packages/*/src --include=*.ts | grep -v dist returns ONLY the resolver definition line

items.title: Migrate the on-disk state directories with history preserved
items.context: git mv .lattice -> .proof-or-stop and .lattice-codex -> .proof-or-stop-codex, using git mv so history follows the files. 7571 tracked files. Verify afterward that story archives still parse, that signatures on historical findings/review-passes still verify (they must, since salts are path-independent), and that gitignore entries, lock paths and discovery files (.lattice-serve.json) were updated. This item is where the story either preserves 326 stories of evidence or destroys it.
items.userSees: `story_get` prints a phase for two NAMED archived stories (one earliest-era, one pre-migration) against .proof-or-stop, and `git show --stat` shows renames only, zero content edits

happy.desc: node bin/proof-or-stop.js session_brief and story_get both succeed against .proof-or-stop after the move

edge.desc: git log --follow on a moved archive file still shows its pre-move history

adversarial.desc: Signature verification passes on TWO named archives from different eras; zero archive file CONTENT differs (git diff -M shows pure renames)

items.title: Rename the config and manifest filenames with a read-both fallback
items.context: lattice.config.json -> proof-or-stop.config.json (236+ source sites) and lattice.json -> proof-or-stop.json. Config discovery must accept the deprecated filename for reading so a teammate branch or an unmigrated project still loads, while init and writes emit only the canonical name. Include the .lattice-codex/lattice.json adapter manifest, which the adapter resolves by exact name.
items.userSees: canonical-only project loads silently; deprecated-only project prints "lattice.config.json is deprecated; use proof-or-stop.config.json" on STDERR while `validate --json` stdout stays single-payload parseable

happy.desc: A project with only proof-or-stop.config.json loads and prints NO deprecation notice

edge.desc: A project with only lattice.config.json loads AND prints a one-line notice on STDERR naming both filenames

adversarial.desc: validate --json stdout still parses as exactly one JSON payload with the deprecated filename present (notice must not leak to stdout)

items.title: Rename the npm package to @proof-or-stop/core
items.context: 4 package.json manifests plus package-lock.json entries and 19 source import sites. This is a published-identity change, distinct in risk from the path renames: any external consumer resolving @lattice/core breaks. Update workspace references, rebuild, and confirm packages/utils (which imports packages/main build output) still resolves. Decide and record whether a deprecated alias package is warranted or whether this is a clean break.
items.userSees: both builds exit 0 with dist present, `node scripts/verify-entrypoints.mjs` prints "entrypoints verified", and root package.json still shows "name": "lattice"

happy.desc: npm --prefix packages/main run build exits 0 AND packages/main/dist/cli-engine.js exists

edge.desc: packages/utils builds too, proving the cross-package import of packages/main dist still resolves under the new name

adversarial.desc: grep for @lattice/core outside node_modules, dist and the state dir returns nothing, and root package.json name is STILL lattice (OQ-2 exclusion intact)

items.title: Remove the deprecated bin aliases and prove nothing depends on them
items.context:
Delete bin/lattice.js and bin/lattice-codex.js. Do this LAST, after the rest is green, because it is the one irreversible break of the multi-developer compatibility guarantee B-cdf6 established. bin/proof-or-stop-codex.js references the codex alias and verify_codex has a check for it; both need updating. Also update the package.json bin map, the pre-push hook's self-repo detection, and CLAUDE.md.

INIT product-reviewer issue (medium): the original form of this item hard-cut the guarantee with NO transition signal, so a teammate would discover the break only when their 'lattice' invocation failed — a silent UX cliff. Amended acceptance: the removal must be ANNOUNCED, not merely performed. Required: a CHANGELOG entry naming both removed aliases and their replacements. PLAN must additionally decide between (a) a deprecation-warning phase where bin/lattice.js prints a visible notice before delegating, held one release cycle before removal, versus (b) immediate removal with the changelog as the only signal — and RECORD which was chosen and why. Option (a) is the reviewer's preference; the operator asked for removal, so the tradeoff is explicit rather than assumed.
items.userSees: `node bin/lattice.js` errors with "Cannot find module", `node bin/proof-or-stop.js --version` prints "Proof-or-Stop 0.3.x", and CHANGELOG.md contains both "bin/lattice.js" and "bin/lattice-codex.js"

happy.desc: node bin/proof-or-stop.js --version prints the version and proof-or-stop codex verify passes after the aliases are gone

edge.desc: node bin/lattice.js exits non-zero with a command-not-found style error rather than a silent no-op

adversarial.desc: CHANGELOG.md names BOTH removed aliases and their replacements, so the break is announced rather than discovered

items.title: Extend the residue gate to enforce the new identities and re-pin affected fingerprints
items.context: The lattice-residue gate currently permits .lattice, lattice.config.json and @lattice/core as FROZEN rows. Flip those rows from exempt to forbidden in product runtime source so the migration cannot silently regress, keeping frozen-by-design tokens (salts, role IDs) exempt with recorded reasons. Also re-pin any canonical AST fingerprints the migration moves; note from B-cdf6 that one fingerprint had TWO coupled copies, so grep the old digest repo-wide before editing either.
items.userSees: `node scripts/verify-lattice-residue.mjs` prints "PASS lattice-residue" for every check; a deliberately reintroduced .lattice literal flips it to a non-zero exit

happy.desc: node scripts/verify-lattice-residue.mjs prints PASS for all checks after the migration

edge.desc: Reintroducing a bare .lattice literal into packages/main/src makes the gate FAIL, proving it is enforcing not merely reporting

adversarial.desc: The two coupled AST fingerprint copies stay in sync: both retired-authority-vocabulary-guard-smoke and verify-process-fact-contract exit 0

items.title: Prove the state-directory move is reversible before performing it
items.context:
INIT-002, raised by the INIT reviewer and matching my own stated uncertainty: CHK-002's read-both resolver gives CODE-level reversibility but not DATA-move reversibility, and nothing covered aborting a partially-completed git mv of ~7574 tracked files. This item supplies the missing half. Establish and rehearse the abort procedure: confirm the move is a single atomic commit that 'git revert' undoes cleanly (git mv preserves content, so a revert restores paths without content loss), verify on a scratch clone that reverting restores story archives to a readable state, and record the exact abort command plus how to detect a half-done state.

SEQUENCING, corrected per INIT-005: this item's ID is CHK-008 because checklist_add appends, so its array POSITION is last — but it is an EXECUTION PREREQUISITE of CHK-003 (the git mv), not a follow-up. An earlier draft of this context claimed it was 'sequenced before CHK-003', which contradicted its own array position and was standalone-visible in checklist.json; that claim is withdrawn. The real ordering is enforced two ways: (1) PLAN must record CHK-003 DependsOn CHK-008 in plan.md, and (2) CHK-003 must not be started until this rehearsal is done and its evidence recorded. ID order is not execution order in this story.
items.userSees: rehearsal transcript shows `story_get` printing an archived story phase both after the move and after `git revert`, plus the exact abort command

happy.desc: On a scratch clone, story_get on an archived story succeeds BOTH after applying the move and after git revert

edge.desc: A deliberately half-done move (one dir moved, one not) is detected by the documented half-done check

adversarial.desc: The move is a single commit: git revert <sha> alone restores the pre-move layout with no manual fixup
